key_insight: Patient-specific respiratory motion can be modeled and rendered via CT-informed Gaussian splatting to create a dynamic, time-varying airway representation that enables accurate bronchoscope-to-CT registration without breath-hold protocols.
problem_solved: Eliminates CT-to-body divergence caused by 5–20 mm respiratory deformation that forces disruptive breath-hold procedures, improving intraoperative localization during bronchoscopy.
method: Build a patient-specific dynamic airway model from preoperative CT plus respiratory phase/signals to capture motion states.
Represent and render the time-varying airway with Gaussian splatting (fast, continuous volumetric rendering) conditioned on respiratory phase.
Register live endoscopic video frames to the dynamic rendered model (rather than a static CT) to recover accurate pose in real time.
impact: Enables robust, real-time medical image registration under physiological motion—reducing workflow disruption and improving localization accuracy—while demonstrating how differentiable volumetric rendering (Gaussian splatting) can be used for dynamic scene modeling in medical AI.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: static CT render vs. CT-informed dynamic Gaussian-splat render showing airway displacement over a breathing cycle.
Pipeline diagram: CT + respiratory signal → dynamic Gaussian splatting renderer → video-to-model registration → pose estimate.
Bar chart or boxplot: localization error (mm) with static CT + breath-hold vs. static CT without breath-hold vs. dynamic model.
Animated sequence or GIF showing bronchoscope view aligning to the dynamic render through a respiration cycle (illustrating no breath-hold needed).
paper_title: Stop Holding Your Breath: CT-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Bronchoscopy
paper_authors: Andrea Dunn Beltran, Daniel Rho, Aarav Mehta, Xinqi Xiong, Raúl San José Estépar
